what_its_for: Dornase alfa is used to help people with cystic fibrosis (CF) breathe more easily. It works by thinning and loosening the thick, sticky mucus that builds up in the lungs, making it easier to cough out. This helps reduce the risk of lung infections and keeps your lungs working better.
how_to_take: Dornase alfa is breathed in (inhaled) as a mist using a special nebulizer machine. You should only use the nebulizer devices recommended by your doctor or pharmacist (such as the PARI LC Plus or Hudson T Up-Draft II nebulizers). Do NOT mix dornase alfa with any other medicines in the nebulizer cup. Before each use, wash your hands well. Pour the entire contents of one single-use ampule into the nebulizer cup. Breathe in the mist slowly and deeply through the mouthpiece until all the medicine is gone. Rinse your mouth with water after each treatment. Clean your nebulizer equipment after every use according to the manufacturer's instructions.
dosing: The usual dose for most patients (adults and children 5 years and older) is ONE ampule (2.5 mg) inhaled once a day. Some patients may benefit from taking it twice a day — your doctor will decide what is best for you. Each ampule contains a single dose and should NEVER be reused. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on that same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. Try to use your nebulizer at the same time each day to help you remember.
storage: Store dornase alfa ampules in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). Keep them in the original foil pouch to protect them from light. Do NOT freeze. If you need to take them with you (for example when traveling), they can be kept at room temperature (up to 77°F / 25°C) and out of direct sunlight for up to 24 hours. Throw away any ampule that appears cloudy or discolored. Keep out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT mix dornase alfa with any other medications in the nebulizer — this can make it stop working. Avoid exposing ampules to bright light or extreme heat. Do not freeze the medication. Do not use an ampule more than once — each ampule is for single use only. Do not skip your other CF treatments (like chest physiotherapy) unless your doctor tells you to, as dornase alfa works best when used together with your full treatment plan.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if you experience any of the following: chest pain or tightness that is new or gets worse, difficulty breathing or wheezing after using the medication, a rash, itching, or signs of an allergic reaction (like swelling of the face, lips, or throat), voice changes or hoarseness that bother you, sore throat or mouth irritation that does not go away, fever, or if you feel your breathing is getting worse instead of better. Seek emergency help immediately if you have severe trouble breathing or signs of a serious allergic reaction.
when_it_works: Dornase alfa starts working relatively quickly to thin the mucus in your lungs. You may notice that it is easier to cough up mucus within the first few days to weeks of starting treatment. However, the full benefits — such as fewer lung infections and improved lung function — may take several weeks to months of regular use to become noticeable. It is very important to keep using it every day, even if you feel well, to get the most benefit.
special_populations: Children: Dornase alfa is approved and considered safe for children with cystic fibrosis who are 5 years of age and older. Children under 5 may sometimes be prescribed it by a specialist, but talk to your doctor. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, tell your doctor before using this medication. Your doctor will help weigh the benefits and risks for you and your baby. Elderly patients: There is limited specific data for older adults with cystic fibrosis, but no special dose adjustments are currently recommended. Always tell your doctor and pharmacist about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you are taking.
